title: Context Is the New Code — Patrick Debois, Tessl
talk_summary: Debois argues agent context (prompts, skills, agent.md) should be engineered like code: generated, tested with evals, distributed as versioned packages, and observed via logs/PR/prod feedback. He emphasizes nondeterministic eval runs, LLM-as-judge with tools in sandboxes, and context filtering for security.

takeaways.technique: Evals for agent context and skills
takeaways.what_they_do: They write evals for prompts/skills/agent.md: format linting, LLM judges against company conventions, and CI-run suites to detect context regressions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you start writing evals for which are tests for your kind of code context

takeaways.technique: LLM judge with tools in sandbox
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of only judging a diff, they give the judge tools so it can execute curl/tests in a sandbox and verify end-to-end behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you give the judge a tool, and the judge becomes an agent, and it can do things in a sandbox and execute stuff.

takeaways.technique: Nondeterministic eval pass rates and error budgets
takeaways.what_they_do: They run evals multiple times and track success rate rather than treating one pass/fail as deterministic, assigning error budgets to critical tests.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you run it five times, and out of five, how many times does it succeed?
takeaways.numbers: run 5 times; success rate out of 5

takeaways.technique: Mine logs/PR/prod feedback into shared context
takeaways.what_they_do: They surface recurring missing-context signals from agent logs, PR feedback, and production failures, then update shared context so everyone benefits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If everybody's missing this piece, we should create context for this.

takeaways.what_they_do: They note sandboxes do not block agent.md/skill.md loading, so they add a context filter/WAF for prompt injection and unsafe patterns in downloaded context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can't filter that with sandboxes. You need to have another way. I call that a context filter.

takeaways.what_they_do: They package reusable context/skills with versions, dependencies, and security metadata so teams can install vetted pieces instead of copy-pasting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what if we package kind of pieces of context, and then we are able to install pieces of context
